records.claim: Freq-HRL reduces responsibility-space lower LF drift without harming return across the registered MuJoCo tasks.
records.allowed_wording: On the frozen v12 protocol, Freq-HRL reduced the registered responsibility-space lower-LF diagnostic and met return noninferiority in HalfCheetah-v5, Hopper-v5, and Walker2d-v5. This result does not establish separation of the pre-routing lower action or the upper-action high-frequency budget.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v12 proves raw behavioral frequency separation or universal no-tradeoff.

records.claim: Freq-HRL simultaneously preserves return, reduces responsibility and raw lower LF drift, and bounds upper HF action power across all registered MuJoCo tasks.
records.allowed_wording: The stricter frozen v13 behavioral claim failed: HalfCheetah-v5 missed the raw lower-LF reduction gate and Hopper-v5 missed the upper-HF budget; Walker2d-v5 passed all registered gates. Return noninferiority and responsibility-space reduction passed in all three tasks.
records.forbidden_wording: Freq-HRL has confirmatory support for raw behavioral frequency separation across all MuJoCo tasks.

records.claim: Freq-HRL outperforms every matched learned baseline on pooled return and lower-LF drift.
records.allowed_wording: Across 24 independent training replicates, eight held-out paths per replicate, and six registered scenarios, Freq-HRL v7.4 supported improvement in 8 of 12 Holm-controlled pooled contrasts. Its return was significantly worse than matched generic HRL-GRU-PPO, while its return contrast with matched SAC and both drift contrasts with generic HRL variants were inconclusive.
records.forbidden_wording: Freq-HRL uniformly dominates all matched PPO, recurrent HRL, SAC, and TD3 baselines.

records.claim: A fixed endpoint-aligned leakage coefficient is behavior-safe across all registered MuJoCo tasks.
records.allowed_wording: The v14 development screen found no fixed endpoint-aligned coefficient that passed all four safety gates in all three MuJoCo tasks; it motivates adaptive or constrained upper-policy training. These outcomes are not confirmatory evidence.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14 supports a positive performance or behavior claim, or supplies held-out confirmation for a later algorithm.

records.claim: Crossed-condition checkpoint selection and upper primal-dual training produce a behavior-safe MuJoCo candidate.
records.allowed_wording: The v14.1 development screen evaluated crossed-condition checkpoint selection, the strongest v14 static arm, and three upper primal-dual rates. No arm passed the preregistered return and behavioral gates in all 15 environment-by-disturbance conditions; every candidate passed zero complete condition gates. These outcomes are development evidence only.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.1 validates behavior-safe upper primal-dual Freq-HRL or supplies confirmatory evidence for any selected arm.

records.claim: Physical-scale leakage costs and a causal lower-action high-pass router produce a behavior-safe MuJoCo candidate.
records.allowed_wording: The v14.2 development screen corrected the leakage-cost scale and showed that full causal high-pass routing reduced raw and responsibility lower-LF drift in every registered environment-by-disturbance condition. No arm was behavior-safe overall: the best arm passed 2 of 15 complete condition gates, full routing harmed return or lower-action activity, and upper primal-dual variants saturated in at least one environment. These outcomes motivate partial-strength routing and are not confirmatory evidence.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.2 validates physical behavioral separation, no-tradeoff, or any selected confirmatory Freq-HRL algorithm.

records.claim: A fixed partial-strength causal lower-action router produces behavior-safe physical separation across the registered MuJoCo conditions.
records.allowed_wording: The v14.3 development screen tested seven fixed partial-strength causal lower-action routers on fresh seeds. Every arm reduced responsibility-space lower-LF drift in all 15 environment-by-disturbance conditions, but no arm jointly passed return and raw-behavior gates everywhere. The best arm passed 4 of 15 complete conditions and 10 of 15 strict raw-drift gates. These outcomes motivate a training-time routing curriculum and are not confirmatory evidence.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.3 validates fixed partial-strength routing, physical no-tradeoff, or any selected confirmatory Freq-HRL algorithm.

records.claim: An observed training-time router homotopy produces behavior-safe physical separation across the registered MuJoCo conditions.
records.allowed_wording: The v14.4 development screen exposed router strength to both policies and tested seven frozen constant or delayed homotopy schedules on fresh seeds. No schedule was behavior-safe across all 15 environment-by-disturbance conditions. The best joint arm passed 3 of 15 complete conditions. The fastest ramp met return noninferiority in 10 of 15 conditions but met responsibility and raw-drift gates in only 5 each, indicating policy compensation rather than stable physical separation. These outcomes motivate paired checkpoint continuation and are not confirmatory evidence.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.4 validates router homotopy, physical no-tradeoff, or any selected confirmatory Freq-HRL algorithm.

records.claim: Paired checkpoint continuation with actor-space proximal constraints produces behavior-safe physical separation across the registered MuJoCo conditions.
records.allowed_wording: The v14.5 development screen started every candidate and its compute-matched direct comparator from the same serialized policy and optimizer state. Actor-space proximal constraints stabilized latent policy movement, and two arms met both raw and responsibility drift gates in all 15 conditions. No arm was behavior-safe overall: every routed arm met return noninferiority in only the five Walker2d conditions, Hopper missed the upper-HF budget, and no arm met the trained-checkpoint gate. This identifies a function-discontinuous router intervention rather than optimizer initialization as the remaining defect.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.5 validates paired proximal routing, physical no-tradeoff, or any selected confirmatory Freq-HRL algorithm.

records.claim: Function-preserving conservative responsibility transfer produces behavior-safe learned frequency separation across the registered MuJoCo conditions.
records.allowed_wording: The v14.6 development screen made lower-to-upper transfer function preserving and excluded untrained checkpoints. Every candidate exactly matched its paired control in selected parameters, latent-policy traces, executed-action traces, rewards, and returns. Strengths at or above 0.075 reduced both registered lower-LF diagnostics in all 15 conditions, but every such arm failed the upper-HF budget in all five Hopper conditions and passed only 10 of 15 complete gates. Because policy parameters and environment behavior were identical across arms, this is a responsibility-coordinate diagnostic rather than evidence of improved learned control.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.6 validates learned behavior-safe Freq-HRL, improves control performance, or supplies a selected algorithm for confirmatory testing.

records.claim: Joint learned projection improves reward and both latent and executed frequency endpoints in MuJoCo.
records.allowed_wording: The v14.7 single-replicate preflight validated pathwise projection calibration and confirmed that learned arms changed actor behavior, but the learned arms used a behavior-robust checkpoint selector while the comparator used mean reward. The result is excluded from algorithm selection.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.7 supports reward improvement, learned frequency separation, no-tradeoff behavior, or any confirmatory candidate.

records.claim: Selector-matched learned projection jointly preserves reward and improves latent lower- and upper-frequency endpoints.
records.allowed_wording: The v14.8 single-replicate HalfCheetah preflight removed the v14.7 comparator and actor-identity confounds. Projection-only calibration was pathwise exact, but no learned arm combined reward preservation with latent lower- and upper-frequency improvement. Equal upper and lower dual rates operated at incompatible cost scales.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.8 supports a learned no-tradeoff result, cross-task generality, reward improvement, or confirmatory evidence.

records.claim: Asymmetric feasibility-aware primal-dual training yields joint deployed frequency separation without reward tradeoff.
records.allowed_wording: The v14.9 HalfCheetah development extension found that one asymmetric arm improved mean return in four modes and reduced latent upper-HF power, but worsened every mean lower-frequency endpoint. The audit showed that stochastic rollout-action constraints did not match deterministic deployment actions.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.9 supports joint learned frequency separation, no-tradeoff behavior, cross-task generality, confirmatory reward improvement, or a submission-ready selected algorithm.

records.claim: Deployment-aligned deterministic frequency projection admits a behavior-safe learned checkpoint.
records.allowed_wording: The source-bound v14.10 preflight validated deterministic deployment-frequency gradients, projection calibration, provenance, and held-out-grid integrity. Every learned arm fell back to the initial checkpoint because single-step corrections were smaller than the registered targets.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.10 supports learned frequency separation, reward improvement, no-tradeoff behavior, cross-task generality, confirmatory evidence, or a selected algorithm.

records.claim: Iterative deterministic projection admits a behavior-safe learned checkpoint.
records.allowed_wording: The source-bound v14.11 preflight showed that iterative deterministic projection increased same-batch frequency reduction without surrogate reward-budget violations. Every learned arm nevertheless selected the fallback because pooled improvements did not satisfy worst-condition reward and frequency ranks.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.11 supports an accepted learned checkpoint, reward improvement, no-tradeoff behavior, cross-task generality, confirmatory evidence, or a selected algorithm.

records.claim: Per-group robust projection admits a behavior-safe learned checkpoint.
records.allowed_wording: The source-bound v14.12 preflight preserved four rollout groups and zero per-group surrogate reward-budget violations, but no arm met every paired reward floor and frequency target at an eligible learned checkpoint.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.12 supports an accepted learned checkpoint, reward improvement, no-tradeoff behavior, cross-task generality, confirmatory evidence, or a selected algorithm.

records.claim: Frozen anchor replay and PPO trust regions close the training-state versus deployment-state gap.
records.allowed_wording: The source-bound v14.13 preflight validated exact projection calibration, frozen anchor replay, and finite-budget PPO trust regions. All learned arms selected the fallback because trained checkpoints still failed unseen-seed closed-loop frequency endpoints.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.13 supports an accepted learned checkpoint, reward improvement, learned frequency separation, statistical evidence, confirmatory evidence, or a selected algorithm.

records.claim: Strict closed-loop actor backtracking admits a behavior-safe learned checkpoint from an infeasible anchor.
records.allowed_wording: The source-bound v14.14 preflight executed the independent closed-loop guard but accepted zero effective actor updates. It identified a feasible-set maintenance rule incorrectly applied at an infeasible starting point.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.14 supports an accepted learned checkpoint, reward improvement, learned frequency separation, statistical evidence, confirmatory evidence, or a selected algorithm.

records.claim: Two-phase closed-loop restoration admits a complete-gate learned checkpoint and authorizes multiseed development.
records.allowed_wording: The source-bound v14.15 HalfCheetah preflight selected the restoration arm with reward tolerance 0.005, eight backtracks, and funnel multiplier 3. It accepted 22 effective joint actor updates, reduced 20 closed-loop frequency violations and continuous violation merit to zero under the reward floor, and passed all five held-out disturbance gates. This single-seed result authorizes a fresh multiseed development screen only.
records.forbidden_wording: MuJoCo v14.15 preflight alone supports statistically reliable reward improvement, robust frequency separation, no-tradeoff behavior, cross-environment generality, confirmatory evidence, or a submission-ready algorithm.

records.claim: Historical raw-only C1-C9 matrix generated before the current independent audit.
records.allowed_wording: This snapshot may be used only to trace historical claim changes. Its individual rows require record-level re-adjudication before manuscript use.
records.forbidden_wording: The historical 1-of-9 count is the current authoritative paper conclusion.

records.claim: Historical paper diagnostics that mixed path, surrogate, native, and small-seed support labels.
records.allowed_wording: This file is retained as a historical diagnostic inventory, not as a manuscript evidence source.
records.forbidden_wording: A path test, three-seed surrogate interval, or mechanism diagnostic in the historical file establishes a confirmatory domain-general result.
